summary: Sampson County forestry lookout: two sources date a 120-foot wood CCC tower to 1937, a 1994 visitor found an Aermotor tower, and a 2025 street view shows the tower.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: 120-foot wood tower erected by the CCC, per two sources; a 1994 visitor found an Aermotor tower instead.
CCC four-room frame house, 31 by 25 feet, completed September 15, 1938 by Camp P-68.
Shown on a 1959 USGS map as the Clinton Lookout Tower.

notes_for_editor: Conflict not resolved: the 1937 CCC wood tower (both sources) and the 1994 Aermotor tower may be one tower with a later replacement, or two towers. The 'North Sampson County' 1937 creosoted timber tower may be the same as the Clinton tower under another name. Status 'standing' rests on a photo caption (2025 street view), not on a site visit. Access is unknown; the site is a Forest Service county headquarters per the 1994 sign. Ownership per both sources is NC Division of Forest Resources (record field 'ownership' is 'unknown' and was not changed). Tower height is not given in any source read. WillhiteWeb's 'Tower Elevation: 140 feet' is an elevation, not a height. WillhiteWeb's photo caption dates the 'North Sampson County Tower' to 1938, against the November 1937 date on the Eastern US Lookouts page; the story does not mention the 1938 date. The story calls the Eastern US Lookouts page a 'North Carolina lookout listing', not a state listing, because it is a third-party compilation.
